propositions: Ticket-directory creation must be atomic to prevent interrupted-write debris: directories created by os.makedirs outside the write lock before the first event file lands leave stranded empty directories flagged by fsck as MISSING_CREATE and FOREIGN_STORE_PATH.

New staging module publishes directory and first event together via one os.rename() under the write lock, using dot-prefixed temp-path convention (.tmp-newticket-<pid>-<uuid>) that is already excluded by existing fsck scanners with zero scanner change.

All dir-then-file sites in the store write path must be converted or explicitly exempted: batch_stage_and_commit, inbound_translate._write_event_file, and dispatch_one BRIDGE_ALERT emission are converted; lock.py, hlc.py, fsck_repair.py, session_log.py, identity.py, trusted_env_cmd.py are exempt because they write outside the tracker or use already-handled mechanisms.

Bounded best-effort sweep of stale staging dirs owned by dead pids respects bug 043f boundary: touches only writer's own staging area, never ticket directories or store data, and uses lock_owner v2 stamp (host+pid-namespace+start-time) to defeat pid recycling.

RED-GREEN test coverage reproduces the debris signature under the old code (MISSING_CREATE and FOREIGN_STORE_PATH findings) and proves the fix eliminates it; crash-before-rename test proves temp paths are invisible to fsck; concurrency and batch tests verify the fix applies to all call sites; byte parity unchanged by canonical serializer routing.

All acceptance criteria verified: AC1 atomicity, AC2 RED reproduction and debris elimination, AC3 unchanged lock discipline, AC4 operator-attested audit of all mkdir sites with reasoned exemptions, AC5 lint/typecheck/suite green on 61b49deaa6 with Verified +1 and LLM-Review +1.
